title: Assistant Professor (Tenure Track) in Macroeconomics (100%)
industry: Economics, Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics (JEL E), Economics and Social Sciences
text:
«A place where knowledge is created» – As a leading business university we set global standards for research and teaching by promoting integrative thought, responsible action and an entrepreneurial spirit of innovation in business and society.
 
Assistant Professor (Tenure Track) in Macroeconomics (100%)

The University of St.Gallen and its School of Economics and Political Science are inviting applications for an Assistant Professorship (Tenure Track) in the field of macroeconomics.
Candidates with a focus in applied macroeconomics are particularly encouraged to apply. Candidates should have (or aim to establish) a promising record of internationally recognized research and show commitment to teaching excellence. Ideal candidates have an emerging track record of internationally recognized research in leading general interest or field journals.
Successful candidates will teach in our Economics or International Affairs programmes. Candidates should have a commitment to academic leadership and citizenship, including contributions to public discourse and outreach activities. Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding is a plus.
The appointment is for 6 years, with an intermediate evaluation after 3 years. Based on the tenure track process, successful candidates can be promoted to a tenured Associate Professor position.
The University of St.Gallen is committed to promoting equal opportunities and an inclusive working culture. We explicitly encourage women and members of underrepresented groups to apply. We offer dual-career and welcome services for newly appointed faculty (and their families).
We seek to fill the position per August 1st, 2027, or by mutual agreement.
Interviews will take place online at the European Job Market for Economists (EJME). Short-listed candidates will then be invited to present their research and have an interview with the hiring committee in St. Gallen in January 2027. For further information, please contact Professor Dr Winfried Koeniger, Chair of the Appointment Committee (facultyposition@unisg.ch).
The application should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching and research statement, list of research papers including publications, identification of the job-market paper, and two reference letters. Candidates should submit their application to the President of the University of St.Gallen, Professor Dr Manuel Ammann online via www.unisg.ch/professorships at the latest by October 31st, 2026.
